description: This pie chart, titled “Distribution of Difficulty,” visually represents the proportional breakdown of difficulty levels within a dataset, with five distinct categories shown as colored slices: “Medium” (reddish-pink, 51.8%), “Hard” (blue, 25.7%), “Easy” (light green, 11.2%), “Very hard” (light orange, 6.5%), and “Very easy” (lavender, 6.5%). Each slice is labeled with its category name and corresponding percentage directly on the chart, and a legend in the top-left corner reiterates these categories along with their absolute counts (e.g., “Medium (725,892)”). The chart’s segments are arranged in descending order of size, starting with the largest “Medium” slice on the left, followed clockwise by “Hard,” “Easy,” “Very hard,” and “Very easy.” All slices are solidly colored without any visual emphasis like being exploded or outlined differently. The chart’s title and the legend provide context for the data, which is presented as a total distribution across these five difficulty levels.
